correctness.rationale: Sorting horizontal coordinates with gaps s,t and ordinate increments alpha,beta gives strict angle inequalities, including st<epsilon^2|alpha beta| and alpha beta<0. In sector s<t with t>>epsilon, substitute z=st/epsilon^2 and ds=epsilon^2 dz/t. At t=epsilon^theta (0<theta<1), continuity of convex vertical-section endpoints implies three ordinate intervals coalesce, and the permitted z length becomes |alpha|min(|alpha|,|beta|) for alpha beta<0. Bounded sections and Jacobian dominate the log t integral; the t~epsilon and t~1 boundary slices contribute no epsilon^2 log-scale mass. The exact fiber integral for one interval is 2 int_0^w int_0^r int_0^r u min(u,v)dvdu dr=w^5/12; the sorted-label factor 6 and symmetric t<s regime yield precisely A^-3 int w^5. Independent SymPy integration recomputed int_0^1 int_0^1 u min(u,v)=5/24 and fiber=1/12, with rectangle/triangle/trapezoid coefficients 1,4/3,28/9 under given normalization. Jensen gives the lower bound, and standard 1D Berwald for concave w gives int w^5<=16 A^5/(3 L^4); affine vanishing widths and constant widths show sharpness. Numerical Sobol tests in packaged code are diagnostic only, never continuum proof.
